record.title: PhysRSI-eval reports five-axis measurements of iterative robot-manipulation improvement
record.summary: Galbot researchers introduce PhysRSI-eval, a five-axis profile separating first-attempt performance, timing of gains, attained scores, physical interaction budget and recovery from early failure. In the main simulation evaluation, the paper reports six model-plus-runtime systems on 18 manipulation tasks: GPT-6 Astra solved 15, GPT-6.1 Sol 12, GPT-6 Sol 7, GPT-5.6 Sol 1, Claude Opus 5.5 13, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 11. The paper reports that final score, early improvement and budget efficiency can diverge, and exploratory associations between public capability scores and the five outcome axes. It also reports Astra workspace interventions and held-out layout tests. All results remain author-reported. The main comparison has one improvement chain per task; the capability analysis covers six systems without independent validation; Astra's ablation/frozen tests cover six tasks, and transfer evidence comprises three cases.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Galbot researchers published PhysRSI-eval, a five-axis evaluation profile for iterative robot-manipulation improvement, on 19 October 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report evaluation of six model-plus-runtime systems over 18 RoboDojo manipulation tasks, with task counts solved by K17 of 15, 12, 7, 1, 13 and 11 respectively for GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across the six evaluated systems, the authors report stronger associations of spatial scores with first-attempt performance and gain timing, and of perception scores with attained performance and later recovery; coding scores had weaker associations in this sample.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In Astra's six-task, two-chain-per-task ablation, the paper reports 15/36 late-round successes with the full workspace and feedback condition versus 3/36 with no history across rounds K4–K6.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent multi-chain replication, repeated physical execution reliability, generalization beyond the tested simulation tasks, or predictive validity for deployment outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent multi-chain reproduction of the PhysRSI-eval comparison or the reported workspace interventions was inspected.
Whether the proposed axes predict real deployment reliability or resource costs has not been established.

brief.importance_rationale: If its measurements and reported patterns generalize, separating outcome, improvement timing and physical interaction cost can change evaluation and deployment decisions in embodied-agent research. The present consequence is notable within robotics research; the reported study is narrow and not independently reproduced.
limitations: The main model comparison uses one improvement chain per task; repeated K0 runs do not estimate variability across complete chains.

The capability association analysis covers six model-plus-configuration systems, uses public benchmark settings that differ from the robot runs, and has no independent validation; the smallest adjusted q-value reported is 0.11.
The workspace ablation and frozen-layout tests cover Astra and six tasks. Cross-task transfer is reported for three cases, not a broad transfer evaluation.
The results come from simulation episodes with native grading; the paper does not establish repeated real-robot execution reliability or deployment transfer.
The authors report a separate Gemini 4 partial run over ten tasks; it is excluded from main 18-task association analyses because its task set differs.
brief.summary: Galbot researchers introduce PhysRSI-eval, a five-axis profile separating first-attempt performance, timing of gains, attained scores, physical interaction budget and recovery from early failure. In the main simulation evaluation, the paper reports six model-plus-runtime systems on 18 manipulation tasks: GPT-6 Astra solved 15, GPT-6.1 Sol 12, GPT-6 Sol 7, GPT-5.6 Sol 1, Claude Opus 5.5 13, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 11. technical.claimed_result: The authors report meaningful differences among six model-plus-runtime systems across 18 RoboDojo manipulation tasks and an Astra ablation in which retained history/workspace channels correspond to more late-round successes than the no-history condition.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper defines the five-axis evaluation and reports its simulation results; reported outcomes have not been independently reproduced.
technical.mechanism: PhysRSI-eval measures first-attempt performance, gain timing, attained success, interaction-budget savings and recovery after early failure as distinct axes under a fixed round/interaction budget.
technical.regime: RoboDojo simulated manipulation tasks, with a separate ten-task Gemini 4 run; Astra workspace tests cover six tasks.
technical.reproducibility: The full paper specifies tasks, metrics and ablation conditions. No independent rerun was inspected; repeated complete chains, additional platforms and physical deployment outcomes remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: The study compares six model-plus-runtime configurations in its main simulation protocol and uses within-Astra workspace ablations; the primary model comparison has one improvement chain per task.

brief.title: PhysRSI-eval reports five-axis measurements of iterative robot-manipulation improvement
brief.why_it_matters: Embodied-agent evaluations that report only eventual task success can hide when improvements arrive, how many physical interactions they consume and which early failures are recovered. The paper proposes measurements that expose those differences and reports task-level results under a bounded simulated manipulation protocol. The evidence supports an author-reported evaluation design and results, not a general conclusion that physical recursive self-improvement is reliable or transfers to deployed robots.
